sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s required by enrollment; mathematics PhD 75 credits beyond bachelor’s. International applicants
eligible. Holistic admission, no UChicago-specific barrier established. [s2] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare transcript scans,3 letters, CV and narrative; indicate funding needs; upload required materials with
application. Do not use UT Dallas-only Quick Admit. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Department discourages contacting individual faculty for admission or funding; direct logistical questions to
graduate program. Research-fit outreach distinct but no supervisor agreement required. [s6]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Application portal checklist/to-do list tracks file; upload all materials for each application. Specific letter
receipt/update/reuse mechanics remain unverified. [s1] [s5]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
2026 catalog checked; standing December 15 schedule for upcoming fall, no 2027-28 funding amount
guarantee. [s2]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL 80(old)/4(new), IELTS 6.5, PTE 67, DET 105; scores<2 years at admission, upload report and agency
official copy. TA has separate English interview/ESL requirements. [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Earned bachelor’s/master’s from accredited English-instruction AND examination institution qualifies.

Completed UChicago degree fits; in-progress exemption not expressly established. International TA screening
remains separate. [s3]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional on current departmental how-to-apply and FAQ; code 6897. Older page limits optionality to 2023,
superseded by current general optional wording. [s1] [s6] [s7]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Older departmental page explicitly not required; current page broadly makes GRE optional without separately
naming Math Subject. Confirm current portal treatment if intending to submit. [s1] [s7]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
Published TA $2,400/month,9 credit fall/spring tuition and university health insurance. Guaranteed paid
months/annual total not established; summer not guaranteed. [s6]
Years of support [Unresolved]
No numerical funding-duration guarantee found; confirm appointment/renewal terms. [s6] [s8]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International TA support available. EEF Scholarship and Dean’s Fellowship limited to U.S.citizen/permanent
resident; NSM McDermott award listed separately. [s7]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Minimum 9 credits/long semester, good standing, usually 20 hours/week duties; semester review and funds
affect reappointment. [s8]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Automatic consideration; no separate support application. Indicate no funding needed at beginning of narrative
if applicable. [s6]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Competitive NSM McDermott PhD admission fellowship; advanced RA and teaching associate positions;
summer funding variable. [s6] [s7]
Application fee [Standing rule]
Application $75 nonrefundable. [s4]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Program-based central waiver restricted to U.S.citizens/permanent residents; UT Dallas students/alumni and
qualifying U.S.military separate routes. UChicago F-1 alone does not qualify; documentation via Applicant
Portal. [s4]

months/duration and commitment date. Khan latest paper date not given; potential additional relevant faculty
require complete audit. [s1] [s6]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Complex geometry
Ronan Conlon
Calabi-Yau metrics, Kähler-Ricci solitons, special holonomy and geometric analysis. [s9]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · New examples of affine Calabi-Yau 3-folds with maximal volume growth
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.

Algebraic geometry and Galois theory
Carlos Arreche
Differential algebraic geometry, differential/difference Galois theory and symbolic computation. [s10]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · A computational approach to rational summability and its applications via discrete residues
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Number theory
Rizwanur Khan
Analytic number theory, automorphic forms and L-functions. [s11]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: undated preprint · The first moment of Dirichlet L-functions over generators of the character group
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Representation theory (combinatorial)
Nathan Williams
Reflection/braid groups, dynamical algebraic combinatorics and combinatorial representation theory. [s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Noncrossing Combinatorics, the Full Twist, and Decategorification of Knot Invariants
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
